title: Finite residue lifts as a coherent diagram and Galois cofinality
statement: Let $(H,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a commutative henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], with residue field $k=H/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-residue-field], and let $K/k$ be a chosen separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure]. Write $I$ for the poset of finite separable intermediate fields $k\subset e\subset K$, ordered by inclusion. There exist commutative $H$-algebras $B_e$, each finite as an $H$-module and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $k$-algebra isomorphisms $r_e:B_e/\mathfrak mB_e\xrightarrow{\sim}e$. Each $B_e$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mB_e$, and $H\to B_e$ is local. For each inclusion $e\subset f$, there is exactly one $H$-algebra map $u_{ef}:B_e\to B_f$ whose reduction, under $r_e,r_f$, is that inclusion; it is local. These maps satisfy $u_{ee}=\mathrm{id}$ and $u_{fg}u_{ef}=u_{eg}$, and $I$ is small and directed. Any two finite etale lifts of an identified residue field $e$ admit exactly one residue-compatible $H$-algebra isomorphism. The full subposet $J\subset I$ of finite Galois extensions of $k$ is directed and cofinal (Galois means separable and normal: the minimal polynomial over $k$ of every element splits in the extension). For any such chosen lift diagram and any commutative $H$-algebra $T$, restriction from cocones on $(B_e)_{e\in I}$ to cocones on $(B_e)_{e\in J}$ is a bijection. Consequently the restricted diagram has canonically the same colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], preserving the $H$-structure and the compatible residue maps to $K$.

proof.text: For any $H$-algebra $B$, identify $k\otimes_H B$ with $B/\mathfrak mB$: the maps are $\bar h\otimes b\mapsto hb\bmod\mathfrak mB$ and $b\bmod\mathfrak mB\mapsto1\otimes b$, which are well defined and inverse by the tensor relations. Each $e\in I$ is a finite separable extension of $k$, so [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-field-lift] gives a module-finite etale $H$-algebra $B_e$ with an identified fibre $r_e:B_e/\mathfrak mB_e\simeq e$. Choose one such pair for each $e$. This is a set-indexed choice: intermediate fields of the fixed field $K$ form a subset of its power set, so $I$ and its inclusion arrows are small.

source.place: Tag 04GK (lemma-henselian-cat-finite-etale), essential surjectivity; Tag 0BSL (remark-construct-sh-from-h), first sentence

proof.text: The ideal $\mathfrak mB_e$ is maximal because its quotient is the nonzero field $e$. Every maximal ideal of the module-finite algebra $B_e$ contains $\mathfrak mB_e$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical]; hence it equals this ideal. Thus $B_e$ is local. The composite $H\to B_e\to e$ is the quotient $H\to k$ followed by the given injective inclusion $k\hookrightarrow e$. Its kernel is $\mathfrak m$, proving that $H\to B_e$ is local.

source.place: Tag 0BSL (remark-construct-sh-from-h), finite etale local extensions; maximal-ideal contraction as in Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), proof of (9) implies (10)

proof.text: For $e\subseteq f$, conjugate the field inclusion by $r_e,r_f$ to obtain the fibre map $r_f^{-1}\circ(e\hookrightarrow f)\circ r_e$. The reduction bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-map-bijective], applied to the finite etale $H$-algebras $B_e,B_f$, gives exactly one lift $u_{ef}$. It is local: for $b\in B_e$, the image $u_{ef}(b)$ belongs to $\mathfrak mB_f$ exactly when the image of $r_e(\bar b)$ in $f$ is zero; injectivity of $e\hookrightarrow f$ makes this equivalent to $b\in\mathfrak mB_e$.

source.place: Tag 04GK (lemma-henselian-cat-finite-etale), full faithfulness; Tag 0BSL (remark-construct-sh-from-h), arrows in the system

proof.text: Reduction commutes with composition, so $u_{ee}$ and $\mathrm{id}_{B_e}$ reduce to the same map, and $u_{fg}\circ u_{ef}$ and $u_{eg}$ both reduce to $e\hookrightarrow g$. Injectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-map-bijective] gives the two coherence identities. For two finite etale lifts $B,B'$ with identified fibre $e$, lift the identity of $e$ in both directions by the same bijection. Their composites reduce to identities, hence are identities. The lift is therefore an isomorphism, and injectivity makes it the unique residue-compatible isomorphism. This also applies to arbitrary choices of the pairs in step 1.

source.place: Tags 04GK (lemma-henselian-cat-finite-etale) and 0BSL (remark-construct-sh-from-h), uniqueness from full faithfulness

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois], applied to the specified separable closure $K/k$, this extension is Galois. Given $e,f\in I$, take the union $S$ of finite $k$-bases of $e$ and $f$, regarded as a finite subset of $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-set-in-finite-galois-subextension] there is a finite Galois intermediate field $g$ containing $S$. Since $g$ contains $k$ and these bases, it contains both $e$ and $f$. Also $k\in J\subseteq I$. This proves that $I$ is nonempty directed, that $J$ is directed (use the same argument for $e,f\in J$), and that every $e\in I$ lies below an object of $J$ (take $f=k$). In particular the upper subposet $\{g\in J:e\subseteq g\}$ is nonempty and directed; this is the required cofinality, not merely a choice of an abstract Galois extension outside $K$.

source.place: Tags 09DT (lemma-normal-closure), 0BMG (lemma-normal-closure-inside-normal), 0EXM (lemma-normal-closure-galois); finite Galois enclosure inside the chosen separable closure

proof.text: Fix a commutative $H$-algebra $T$. A cocone on $J$ is a compatible family $a_g:B_g\to T$ of $H$-algebra maps [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For $e\in I$, choose $g\in J$ above $e$ and set $a_e=a_g\circ u_{eg}$. If $g'$ is another choice, take $h\in J$ above both; cocone compatibility and the coherence identities give $a_g u_{eg}=a_h u_{gh}u_{eg}=a_hu_{eh}=a_{g'}u_{eg'}$. Thus $a_e$ is independent of the choice. For $e\subseteq f$, choose $g\in J$ above $f$; then $a_fu_{ef}=a_gu_{fg}u_{ef}=a_gu_{eg}=a_e$. For $e\in J$ the choice $g=e$ gives the original $a_e$. Conversely, an $I$-cocone must satisfy this extension formula for every $e\subseteq g$ with $g\in J$. Extension and restriction are inverse, proving the stated bijection.

source.place: Tag 002F (definition-colimit), cocone compatibility; explicit directed-cofinal extension argument using step 5

proof.text: The two small diagrams have colimits in commutative $H$-algebras by [lem-weil-pbc-commutative-algebras-colimits-exist]. Restrict the universal $I$-cocone to $J$. Given a $J$-cocone, step 6 extends it uniquely to $I$, and the universal $I$-property then supplies exactly one mediating $H$-algebra map. Hence the restricted cocone is a colimit by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Uniqueness of colimits gives the canonical isomorphism with any chosen $J$-colimit; its composites with the $J$-legs are the $I$-legs. These are $H$-algebra maps, so the isomorphism preserves the $H$-structure. Finally define $\rho_e:B_e\to K$ as quotient, then $r_e$, then $e\hookrightarrow K$. The defining reduction of $u_{ef}$ says $\rho_f u_{ef}=\rho_e$. This is a cocone with vertex $K$, and the universal properties just proved show that the two induced maps to $K$ commute with the canonical colimit isomorphism. Thus the compatible residue maps are preserved as asserted.

lean.statement: theorem exists_henselian_residue_lift_diagram (H K : Type u) [CommRing H] [HenselianLocalRing H] [Field K] [Algebra (IsLocalRing.ResidueField H) K] [IsSepClosure (IsLocalRing.ResidueField H) K] : ∃ D : {e : IntermediateField (IsLocalRing.ResidueField H) K // FiniteDimensional (IsLocalRing.ResidueField H) e} ⥤ CommAlgCat.{u} H, ∃ q : ∀ e, D.obj e →+* e.val, (∀ e, Module.Finite H (D.obj e)) ∧ (∀ e, Algebra.Etale H (D.obj e)) ∧ (∀ e, Function.Surjective (q e)) ∧ (∀ e, RingHom.ker (q e) = (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal H).map (algebraMap H (D.obj e))) ∧ (∀ e h, q e (algebraMap H (D.obj e) h) = algebraMap (IsLocalRing.ResidueField H) e.val (IsLocalRing.residue H h)) ∧ (∃ loc : ∀ e, IsLocalRing (D.obj e), (∀ e, @IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (D.obj e) _ (loc e) = (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal H).map (algebraMap H (D.obj e))) ∧ (∀ e, IsLocalHom (algebraMap H (D.obj e)))) ∧ (∀ {e f} (t : e ⟶ f) b, (q f ((D.map t).hom b) : K) = (q e b : K)) ∧ (∀ {e f} (t : e ⟶ f), IsLocalHom (D.map t).hom.toRingHom) ∧ (∀ {e f} (t : e ⟶ f) (g : D.obj e →ₐ[H] D.obj f), (∀ b, (q f (g b) : K) = (q e b : K)) → g = (D.map t).hom)
